user.title: Set up Climate Entity Builder
user.description: Creates a Climate Entity Builder hub. You can set up more than one, e.g. one per floor - each hub has its own independent set of custom preset profiles, offered only to the thermostats added under that hub. Afterwards, use "Add thermostat" and "Add profile" on the hub's device page.

data_description.name: Only used to tell hubs apart on the integrations page.

user.title: Add thermostat
user.description: Build a virtual room thermostat from existing sensors and a switch.

data.name: Name
data.sensor_stale_timeout: Failsafe delay after invalid sensor reading

data_description.name: Name of the thermostat. It becomes the device name and the entity id, e.g. "Bedroom" gives climate.bedroom.
data_description.area_id: Assigns the device to this area once, right now. Changing it later here has no effect if you've since reassigned the device manually on its own page - that manual choice always wins.
data_description.temperature_sensor: The sensor that measures the room temperature (device class temperature).
data_description.temperature_offset: Added to every reading of the temperature sensor before it is shown and used for control, e.g. -0.5 if the sensor reads half a degree too warm. The failsafe plausibility bounds below still judge the raw reading.
data_description.heater: Turned on/off via the generic homeassistant.turn_on/turn_off services.
data_description.humidity_sensor: Optional. Its value is shown as the humidity on the thermostat; it has no effect on heating.
data_description.humidity_offset: Added to every reading of the humidity sensor before it is shown, e.g. -5 if it reads 5 % too high. The result is kept within 0-100 %.
data_description.min_temp: Lowest target temperature that can be set on this thermostat.
data_description.max_temp: Highest target temperature that can be set on this thermostat.
data_description.sensor_stale_timeout: How long an unavailable/unknown/implausible reading is tolerated before the heater is forced off.
data_description.sensor_min_valid_temp: Readings below this value are treated as implausible.
data_description.sensor_max_valid_temp: Readings above this value are treated as implausible.

data_description.target_temp_step: Step size of the target temperature buttons on the thermostat card.
data_description.cold_tolerance: The heater switches on once the room is this many degrees below the target.
data_description.hot_tolerance: The heater switches off once the room is this many degrees above the target. In between, the heater stays as it is.

data.window_open_delay: Delay before pausing after a window opens (optional)

data_description.window_sensors: While any of these is open, heating pauses and switches to the window-open temperature below instead of the normal setpoint.
data_description.window_open_delay: Ignores a brief opening; heating only pauses once a window has stayed open this long.
data_description.window_open_temperature: Target temperature while paused for an open window.

data_description.schedule_entity: A schedule.* entity. When active, the comfort temperature is used; otherwise the eco temperature.
data_description.comfort_temperature: Target temperature in auto mode while the schedule is on, and when the Comfort preset is selected.
data_description.eco_temperature: Target temperature in auto mode while the schedule is off, and when the Eco preset is selected.

user.title: Add profile
user.description: Define a custom preset: a name and a temperature. It's offered as an extra preset (alongside comfort/eco) on every thermostat under this hub, but only while a thermostat is in heat mode.

data_description.name: Shown as the preset's name on every thermostat under this hub, e.g. "Boost" or "Vacation". Can't be one of the built-in preset names (none/comfort/eco/window_open).
data_description.temperature: Applied as the target temperature the moment this preset is selected on a thermostat.
data_description.icon: Shown on a thermostat itself while this profile is its active preset - not in the preset picker's own list, which can't show a custom icon for a dynamically-named preset.

data_description.name: Shown as the preset's name on every thermostat under this hub. Can't be one of the built-in preset names (none/comfort/eco/window_open).

data_description.icon: Shown on a thermostat itself while this profile is its active preset - not in the preset picker's own list, which can't show a custom icon for a dynamically-named preset.
